project: Build Your Own Social Media Post Scheduler
summary: A TypeScript library (zero runtime dependencies, in memory) implementing the core of a social media post scheduler (Buffer/Postiz style), built in one stage following this repo's 21-notification and 22-messaging philosophy exactly: fake providers only, nothing is ever really sent over a network. A channel is just a string key into a FakeChannelProvider map the caller supplies at construction -- schedulePost rejects any channel with no registered provider (UNKNOWN_CHANNEL) at request time. Scheduling is idempotent via a caller-supplied clientRequestId: the same id with the same (content, channel-set, scheduledAt) fingerprint returns the original post and creates nothing new, a different fingerprint is IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. Unlike 22-messaging stage 2, where a real await before the commit meant a plain map lookup could not dedupe truly concurrent duplicates and a synchronous placeholder claim was required, schedulePost here is fully synchronous end to end (no await anywhere on that path), so a plain check-then-set is already safe -- a deliberate, documented contrast rather than an oversight. One post fans out to N independent ChannelDelivery records, one per channel, each with its own status (pending -> sent | dead_letter | canceled, with deliberately no separate failed status since a retryable failure just stays pending) and its own attempt count -- one channel's provider failing, throwing, or exhausting retries never touches a sibling's counters or status, of the same post or any other. tick() polls for due (scheduledAt <= now, driven by an injected Clock, never a real timer) and pending channels and dispatches each independently; a failed attempt retries with exponential backoff (capped) up to maxAttempts, after which that one channel dead-letters permanently. cancelChannel/cancelPost work on any still-pending channel including one mid-retry; editPost is deliberately stricter, requiring zero attempts on every non-canceled channel, because content lives on the post as a whole (not per channel) and a provider that already saw one attempt cannot have that attempt un-seen. attempts is incremented synchronously immediately before tick()'s one await, which is what lets editPost detect an in-flight send without an extra guard; cancelChannel/cancelPost have no such signal (status stays pending throughout a send) and instead use an explicit dispatching guard (DISPATCH_IN_PROGRESS) that also prevents two overlapping tick() calls from dispatching the same due channel twice -- proven with a dedicated test file using a provider whose promise is resolved by hand, since every other fake provider resolves immediately and would never exercise that path. 84 tests total, including a randomized invariant test (5 seeds x 250 operations across many posts and three provider behaviors, settled to a fixed point and checked for consistency). Mutation checks: 35 total, 31 caught on the first run, 4 real gaps found and closed (editPost's canceled-channel skip was never actually exercised because the existing test canceled before any attempt; the constructor's own retry-policy validation had zero tests) -- all 35 now caught. Not built: a distinction between retryable and permanent provider failures, per-channel content length limits, a job queue with leases for multiple concurrent dispatch workers, idempotency key expiry, editing the channel list itself, an HTTP API.

pitch.intro_30s: Maine ek social media post scheduler ka core banaya hai, Buffer/Postiz jaisa, TypeScript mein, in memory. Fake providers ka istemal hota hai -- koi real LinkedIn/Twitter API call kabhi nahi hota, exactly 21-notification wali philosophy. Ek post multiple channels ko target karta hai, har channel ka apna independent status aur retry count hota hai -- ek channel fail ho to doosra affected nahi hota. Idempotent scheduling, exponential backoff retry, per-channel dead-letter, aur cancel/edit guards. 84 tests, 35 mutation checks, sab caught.
pitch.explain_2min:
'Build your own Buffer' ek realistic LLD prompt hai jo kahin bhi aata hai jab system ko FUTURE TIME par kuch karna ho, independently, per target, retries ke saath -- same shape ek cron-jaisi job runner, webhook delivery system, ya multi-region deployment fan-out ki.

Channel sirf ek string key hai, ek FakeChannelProvider map mein -- scheduler ko pata hi nahi hota channel ASLI mein kya hai, sirf yeh ki kuch registered hai usse handle karne ke liye. Idempotency clientRequestId se -- par yahan interesting baat yeh hai ki koi SYNCHRONOUS claim ki zaroorat nahi hai, 22-messaging stage 2 ke ulta: schedulePost() poora synchronous hai, koi await nahi, isliye ek plain check-then-set already safe hai kyunki JavaScript poora function body ek hi turn mein chalata hai.

Ek post N channels ko target karta hai, har ek ko apna independent ChannelDelivery milta hai -- status enum sirf chaar values: pending -> sent | dead_letter | canceled. Deliberately koi alag 'failed' status nahi hai -- ek retry-bachi-hui failure sirf 'pending' rehta hai, sirf attempts exhaust hone par 'dead_letter' terminal hota hai.

tick() ek poll hai, job queue with leases nahi -- stage 1 mein ek hi caller dispatch drive karta hai, isliye lease (jo DOOSRE caller ko job 'steal' karne deta) ki zaroorat nahi. Ek lightweight 'dispatching' set same caller ke apne overlap (jaise ek slow provider ke beech ek cancel ya doosra tick()) ke against protect karta hai.

attempts SYNCHRONOUSLY increment hota hai await se PEHLE -- isse editPost ek in-flight send ko bina extra guard ke detect kar leta hai. cancelChannel/cancelPost ke paas yeh signal nahi hai, isliye woh 'dispatching' guard use karte hain. 84 tests, 35 mutation checks, sab caught.
pitch.deep_5min:
Ek post ki journey, 3 channels tak, ek flaky retry, aur ek cancel.

Scheduling. Caller schedulePost({clientRequestId, content, channels: ['linkedin','twitter','mastodon'], scheduledAt}) call karta hai. Yeh poora SYNCHRONOUS hai -- validation (content length, channel list non-empty/no-duplicates/all-registered, scheduledAt, clientRequestId shape), phir idempotency map check (clientRequestId already hai? fingerprint match? -- IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT agar mismatch), phir ek SocialPost record banta hai apne teen ChannelDelivery records ke saath, har ek status='pending', attempts=0. Koi await yahan nahi hai, isliye ek plain map.has()/map.set() hi kaafi hai dedupe ke liye -- 22-messaging stage 2 ke contrast mein, jahan ek REAL await commit se pehle tha, isliye ek synchronous PLACEHOLDER claim zaroori thi N concurrent identical sends ko N messages banne se rokne ke liye. Yahan woh problem exist hi nahi karti.

tick() -- pehli baar. clock.now() abhi scheduledAt se pehle hai -- tick() kuch nahi karta, sab teen channels 'pending attempts=0' rehte hain.

tick() -- clock advance karne ke baad. Ab scheduledAt paar ho gaya hai. tick() har due+pending channel ke liye dispatchChannel() call karta hai, ek saath (Promise.all style, par ek channel ka throw doosre ko affect nahi karta). linkedin ka AlwaysSucceedsProvider turant succeed karta hai -- attempts=1, status='sent', providerId/sentAt record hote hain. twitter ka FlakyProvider(2) pehle 2 attempts fail karta hai -- attempts=1, status still 'pending' (yeh terminal nahi hai), lastError set, nextAttemptAt = now + backoffMs(1). mastodon ka AlwaysFailsProvider bhi fail karta hai -- same shape, attempts=1, pending, backoff mein.

tick() -- backoff ke beech mein. Clock thoda advance hota hai, par nextAttemptAt se kam -- tick() twitter/mastodon ko touch nahi karta (abhi due nahi hain), linkedin already terminal hai toh usse bhi nahi.

tick() -- backoff ke baad. twitter ka 2nd attempt (abhi bhi FlakyProvider ke failCount ke andar) fail hota hai, attempts=2, backoff double hota hai (capped maxBackoffMs par). mastodon ka 2nd attempt bhi fail -- attempts=2.

tick() -- final. twitter ka 3rd attempt succeed karta hai (FlakyProvider ne sirf 2 bar fail karna tha) -- status='sent', attempts=3. mastodon ka 3rd attempt bhi fail hota hai, par ab attempts === maxAttempts (3) -- status='dead_letter' PERMANENTLY, koi future tick() isse kabhi touch nahi karega (assert hota hai provider call count unchanged rehta hai).

Cancel. Ek naya post schedule hota hai 2 channels ke saath. cancelChannel(postId, 'twitter') call hota hai USSE PEHLE jo tick() dispatch kare -- status='canceled' ban jaata hai turant (synchronous), koi dispatching guard trigger nahi hoti kyunki kuch bhi in-flight nahi tha. Jab tick() baad mein chalta hai, canceled channel ko skip kar diya jaata hai, kabhi provider ko call nahi kiya jaata.

Edit vs cancel ka asymmetry. Agar koi channel ka attempts > 0 ho (chahe woh abhi bhi 'pending' ho, retry ka intezaar kar raha ho), editPost() is post par POST_ALREADY_DISPATCHED throw karta hai -- content ek single field hai poore post par, per channel nahi, isliye half-edited content ka koi tarika nahi hai express karne ka. Par cancelChannel ussi 'pending, attempts>0' channel ko bina kisi problem ke cancel kar sakta hai -- cancel karne ke liye kuch 'undo' karne ki zaroorat nahi, sirf future attempt ko hone se rokna hai.

Dispatch-in-flight race. Ek provider ka promise MANUALLY resolve hota hai (test-only), aur usi waqt cancelChannel() call hota hai jab tick() uska await abhi chal raha hai -- dispatching guard (DISPATCH_IN_PROGRESS) is race ko catch karta hai, kyunki attempts already-incremented signal yahan nahi dikhta jab tak await resolve na ho.
pitch.architecture_walkthrough: src/clock.ts: injectable Clock (systemClock/ManualClock), same shape as 22-messaging. src/errors.ts: SchedulerError, error codes (UNKNOWN_CHANNEL, IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, CHANNEL_NOT_PENDING, NOTHING_PENDING, POST_ALREADY_DISPATCHED, DISPATCH_IN_PROGRESS). src/types.ts: SocialPost, ChannelDelivery, ProviderResult. src/providers.ts: FakeChannelProvider interface, AlwaysSucceedsProvider, AlwaysFailsProvider, FlakyProvider(failCount) (fails first K attempts per (postId,channel) independently). src/scheduler.ts: sabse bada file -- SocialScheduler class: schedulePost (validation, idempotency, fan-out), tick (due detection, dispatch, retry/backoff/dead-letter), cancelChannel/cancelPost, editPost, dispatchChannel (private, the one await), dispatching guard. src/demo.ts: npm run demo -- multi-channel post, mixed outcomes (sent/flaky-retried/dead-lettered/canceled). test/: 6 files -- schedule (35), tick (12), cancel-edit (22), dispatch-guard (3, manually-resolved provider), providers (7), invariants (5 randomized seeds).
difficult_decisions: Idempotency ko koi SYNCHRONOUS claim nahi chahiye, sirf ek plain check-then-set. 22-messaging stage 2 se deliberate contrast -- wahan ek REAL await commit se pehle tha, isliye N truly concurrent sends map-lookup ko miss kar sakte the pehle commit se pehle. Yahan schedulePost() poora synchronous hai (no await), isliye JavaScript function-body-ek-turn-mein-chalta-hai guarantee hi kaafi hai.

Ek status enum, do nahi -- pending/sent/dead_letter/canceled, koi alag 'failed' status nahi. Ek 'failed' status 'dead_letter' ke paas sirf 'pending' kehne ka doosra tarika hota -- is repo ka rule hai 'a status field with guarded transitions is enough'.

Per-channel fan-out -- ek independent ChannelDelivery per channel, plain object mein keyed. 22-messaging ke per-recipient receipt map jaisi reasoning: 'delivered' ek (post, channel) pair ki property hai, sirf post ki nahi.

tick() ek POLL hai, job queue with leases nahi. Stage 1 mein ek hi caller dispatch drive karta hai, kabhi doosre workers job 'steal' nahi karte -- lease ki zaroorat nahi. Ek lightweight 'dispatching' set same caller ke apne overlap ke against kaafi hai.

cancelChannel/cancelPost 'still pending' rule use karte hain; editPost STRICTER hai -- zero attempts on every non-canceled channel. Content ek field hai poore post par (per channel nahi), isliye ek provider jisne already ek attempt dekha hai, uska attempt un-see nahi ho sakta -- ek half-edited post alag channels ko alag text dikhayega bina express karne ka tarika.

attempts SYNCHRONOUSLY increment hota hai await se PEHLE -- yahi signal editPost ko in-flight detect karne deta hai bina extra guard ke. cancelChannel/cancelPost ke paas yeh signal nahi (status pending hi rehta hai), isliye explicit 'dispatching' guard.
biggest_challenges: E3 mutation survivor: editPost ka 'canceled'-skip hatane se existing test pass ho gaya kyunki woh test channel ko attempts===0 par hi cancel karta tha -- attempts>0 check kabhi dekh hi nahi raha tha usse. Naya test: ek channel ko MID-RETRY cancel karo (ek failed attempt ke baad, status abhi 'pending'), phir post edit karo -- yeh specifically canceled-skip ko exercise karta hai.

K1/K2/K3 mutation survivors: constructor ke retry-policy validations (maxAttempts>=1, initialBackoffMs>=0, maxBackoffMs>=initialBackoffMs) ke liye KOI test hi nahi tha. Ek poora naya describe block add karna pada.

Dispatch-in-flight race ko test karna -- har fake provider turant resolve hota hai, isliye koi existing test kabhi genuinely overlap karta hi nahi tha. Ek dedicated test file (dispatch-guard.test.ts) banana pada jahan provider ka promise MANUALLY resolve hota hai, taaki cancel/doosra tick() beech mein genuinely race kar sake.
failure_scenarios: Ek channel ka provider repeatedly fail kare: exponential backoff se retry hota hai maxAttempts tak, phir SIRF woh channel 'dead_letter' ban jaata hai -- koi future tick() isse touch nahi karega, doosre channels affected nahi hote.

Ek provider throw kare (crash, not just a rejected result): yeh ek failed attempt treat hota hai, crash nahi -- normal retry/backoff/dead-letter path se guzarta hai, aur tick()'s batch ya doosre channels ko affect nahi karta.
Koi cancelChannel call kare jabki ek send abhi in-flight hai (provider ka promise pending): DISPATCH_IN_PROGRESS error, koi state change nahi -- caller ko retry karna padega send settle hone ke baad.

Do overlapping tick() calls same due channel ko dispatch karne ki koshish karen: dispatching guard dono mein se ek ko hi actually provider call karne deta hai, doosra same due channel ko dobara touch nahi karta.
Caller ek already-dispatched (attempts>0) channel wala post edit karne ki koshish kare: POST_ALREADY_DISPATCHED, kuch nahi badalta -- 'an error means nothing happened'.
Caller SAME clientRequestId ko ALAG content/channels/scheduledAt ke saath resend kare: IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, original post untouched rehta hai.
improvements: Retryable vs permanent provider failure ka distinction nahi hai -- har failure maxAttempts tak retry hoti hai phir dead-letter, chahe woh ek permanent failure ho (jaise invalid credentials) jo kabhi retry se succeed nahi hogi.
Per-channel content length limit nahi hai -- ek hi MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH sab channels ke liye, jabki real platforms (Twitter ka short-form vs LinkedIn ka long-form) bahut alag hote hain.
Job queue with leases nahi hai multiple concurrent dispatch workers ke liye -- tick() ek hi implicit caller assume karta hai.
Idempotency keys kabhi expire nahi hote -- memory traffic ke saath grow karti hai, koi TTL ya size cap nahi.
Channel list khud edit karna supported nahi hai -- channel add/remove karne ke liye us channel ko cancel karo aur naya post schedule karo.
HTTP API nahi hai -- yeh ek plain library hai, same shape jo 21/22 ke stage 1 hain.

learning_path.concept: Per-channel fan-out: why one status per channel, not one per post
steps: 1. Concept: ek post N channels ko target karta hai -- har channel ka apna independent ChannelDelivery hai, apna status/attempts/nextAttemptAt ke saath.

2. Project need: agar ek single status poore post par hota, ek channel ka fail hona poore post ko 'failed' dikha deta chahe doosre channels succeed ho gaye hon -- 'delivered' ek (post, channel) PAIR ki property hai, sirf post ki nahi.
3. Code/API: src/types.ts ChannelDelivery; src/scheduler.ts schedulePost (fan-out), tick (per-channel dispatch).
4. Detail: ek channel ka provider fail/throw/dead-letter kabhi doosre channel ke counters ya status ko touch nahi karta -- dedicated tests isse directly assert karte hain.
5. Demo: cd projects/26-social-scheduler && npx vitest run test/tick.test.ts -t 'independence' -- 'one succeeds while a sibling fails-then-retries-then-succeeds'.
6. Interviewer next: agar ek post 100 channels target kare, per-channel map kis point par ek alag data structure maangega?

learning_path.concept: Idempotent scheduling without a synchronous claim: contrast with messaging stage 2
steps: 1. Concept: clientRequestId se idempotency -- same id+fingerprint original return karta hai, alag fingerprint IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. schedulePost() poora SYNCHRONOUS hai, koi await nahi.

2. Project need: 22-messaging stage 2 mein ek REAL await commit se pehle tha, isliye plain map-lookup N truly concurrent duplicates ko miss kar sakta tha -- ek synchronous PLACEHOLDER claim zaroori thi. Yahan woh problem exist nahi karti kyunki pura path synchronous hai.
3. Code/API: src/scheduler.ts schedulePost (idempotency map check-then-set, no await before it).
4. Detail: yeh ek DELIBERATE design decision hai, documented in PLAN.md, messaging ke stage 2 se explicitly contrast karte hue -- oversight nahi.
5. Demo: cd projects/26-social-scheduler && npx vitest run test/schedule.test.ts -t 'idempot' -- replay, conflict, channel-order-independence tests.
6. Interviewer next: agar schedulePost() KABHI ek await add kare (jaise ek DB write), is idempotency scheme mein kya badalna padega?

learning_path.concept: Retry with exponential backoff and per-channel dead-lettering
steps: 1. Concept: ek failed attempt retries hota hai exponential backoff se (capped), maxAttempts tak. Exhaust hone par SIRF woh channel 'dead_letter' ban jaata hai, permanently.

2. Project need: ek temporarily-down provider (jaise mastodon instance down) ko bina rukte retry karna chahiye, par forever nahi -- aur ek dead channel ko future tick() calls kabhi touch nahi karna chahiye (wasted provider calls).
3. Code/API: src/scheduler.ts dispatchChannel (backoffMs formula), tick (due+pending filter).
4. Detail: backoffMs(attempt) = min(maxBackoffMs, initialBackoffMs * 2^(attempt-1)) -- Clock se driven, kabhi real sleep nahi.
5. Demo: cd projects/26-social-scheduler && npx vitest run test/tick.test.ts -t 'dead' -- 'exhausts attempts, never retried again, does not affect a sibling channel'.
6. Interviewer next: agar backoff delay ko jitter bhi chahiye (thundering herd avoid karne ke liye), kahan add karoge?

learning_path.concept: cancel vs edit: why editing is the stricter rule
steps: 1. Concept: cancelChannel/cancelPost kaam karte hain koi bhi STILL-PENDING channel par, chahe woh mid-retry ho. editPost STRICTER hai -- zero attempts on every non-canceled channel zaroori hai.

2. Project need: content ek SINGLE field hai poore post par, per channel nahi -- ek provider jisne already ek attempt dekha hai (chahe fail hua ho), uska attempt un-see nahi ho sakta. Ek half-edited post alag channels ko alag text dikhayega.
3. Code/API: src/scheduler.ts cancelChannel, cancelPost, editPost.

4. Detail: cancel ke liye kuch 'undo' nahi karna -- ek provider call jo kabhi shuru nahi hua, use start hone se rokna hai. Edit different hai -- jo already tried ho gaya, usse wapas nahi liya ja sakta.
5. Demo: cd projects/26-social-scheduler && npx vitest run test/cancel-edit.test.ts -t 'canceled mid-retry' -- 'allows editing around a canceled channel incl. one canceled mid-retry'.
6. Interviewer next: agar content per-channel ban jaaye (jaise Twitter ke liye short version, LinkedIn ke liye long), yeh edit restriction kaise badlegi?

learning_path.concept: In-flight protection without a job queue: the dispatching guard
steps: 1. Concept: tick()'s sirf ek await provider.send() hai. attempts SYNCHRONOUSLY increment hota hai is await se PEHLE -- editPost isi se 'already tried' detect kar leta hai. cancelChannel/cancelPost ke paas yeh signal nahi hai (status pending hi rehta hai), isliye 'dispatching' set use karte hain.

2. Project need: ek slow provider ke beech, ek cancel ya ek doosra tick() call genuinely overlap kar sakta hai same channel ke saath. Bina guard ke, dono double-dispatch ya corrupt state create kar sakte.
3. Code/API: src/scheduler.ts dispatching set, DISPATCH_IN_PROGRESS.

4. Detail: yeh guard same SAME caller ke apne overlap ke against hi protect karta hai -- multiple WORKER processes ek SHARED scheduler par tick() call karen, yeh supported nahi (job queue/lease design chahiye hoga, project 21 jaisa).
5. Demo: cd projects/26-social-scheduler && npx vitest run test/dispatch-guard.test.ts -- manually-resolved provider se race proven.
6. Interviewer next: agar multiple worker processes SAME scheduler ko drive karen, is dispatching set ki jagah kya design chahiye hoga?

learning_path.concept: Testing honestly: randomized invariants and mutation checks
steps: 1. Concept: randomized invariant test = many posts, many channels, mix of providers aur cancellations, settled to a fixed point, checked against consistency rules. Mutation check = ek line todo, suite chalao, check caught ya nahi, file restore karo.
2. Project need: cancel x retry x dead-letter x edit ke combinations haath se likhe tests cover nahi karte poori tarah.
3. Code/API: test/invariants.test.ts (5 seeds x 250 ops), README.md ki mutation table.

4. Detail: 35 mutation checks, 31 first-run caught, 4 genuine gaps (E3: editPost's canceled-skip sirf incidentally covered tha; K1/K2/K3: constructor validation ke zero tests the) -- sab precise new tests se close kiye gaye.
5. Demo: cd projects/26-social-scheduler && npm test (84 tests), aur npx vitest run test/invariants.test.ts.
6. Interviewer next: ek mutation jo 'harmless' lage kisi existing test ke against, par ek REAL gap reveal kare kisi doosre scenario mein -- yeh kaise systematically dhoondhte?
